The 245/75 R16 is the taller, softer and more off-road capable of the two, while the 265/65 R17 is wider and more highway oriented.

faq.q: What pressure should a Fortuner run on 265/65 R17?
faq.a: 30 PSI at the front and 32 PSI at the rear, measured cold. Increase the rear to 35 PSI or more when the vehicle is fully loaded with seven passengers and luggage. A full-size 4x4 is heavy and the rear axle carries most of that load, so under-inflation there is the fastest route to casing failure.

faq.q: Can I use 245/75 R16 instead of 265/65 R17 on my Fortuner?
faq.a: The overall diameters are close - 711 mm against 682 mm - but the Fortuner uses 17-inch rims and a 6-stud pattern, so the 245/75 R16 would require 16-inch rims and a different bolt pattern. It is not a straight swap. Within the 17-inch family, a 255/65 R17 is the common alternative if you want a slightly narrower tyre.

faq.q: How long do 4x4 tyres last in Vapi?
faq.a: On mixed tarmac and broken road running, a good all-terrain pattern in this size gives roughly 50,000 to 70,000 km, and less if the vehicle spends a lot of time off the tarmac. Rotating every 8,000 to 10,000 km and keeping the pressure correct is what makes the difference, because the rear axle does most of the work on a 4x4.
